answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable token as collateral before it may bid or earn. A registry records the lock, while atlas, vine, and comet each build reputation only through completed trades with distinct counterparties; copying an identity cannot copy that history. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock collateral for every persona, tying up capital and risking forfeiture when those personas default or collude under the system’s slashing rules.
